Layer 1 – The last mile

Last mile refers to technologies that connect end users to the internet

Pick a last-mile technology.

Carrier access line

  • Connects you to the internet service provider (ISP), which is an organization or firm that provides access to the internet.
  • Usually provided by local telephone or cable TV carrier and ISP (e.g., Comcast, Verizon, AT&T, …)
  • Last mile technologies: Cable broadband, DSL, Fiber, Wireless (3G, 4G/LTE)

Layer 1 – Some more terminology

Local Area Networks (LAN)

Access to individual computers (e.g., in one building, university)

ISP networks

Connection from backbone to local areas (typically providing access to consumers)

Backbone network (“the wire”)

High-speed data lines that interconnect and collectively form the core of the internet. Owned by large service providers (AT&T, Level3, etc.)

INSY 2299 · Session 12
Layer 2 · TCP/IP

Layer 2 – TCP/IP protocols – packetizing and forwarding

TCP (Transmission control protocol): Works at both ends of internet communication to ensure a perfect copy of a message is sent.

IP (Internet protocol): Routing protocol that is in charge of forwarding packets on the internet.

Packets: Unit of data forwarded by a network. All internet transmissions are divided into packets.

Routers: Computing device that connects networks and exchanges data between them.

INSY 2299 · Session 12
Layer 2 · TCP/IP

Layer 2 – Travelling speed of packages

Bandwidth refers to data transmission speeds

Bandwidth is often expressed in terms of bits per second (bps)

Bits per second is the basic unit of capacity for telecommunications

Other units of expression include:

kbps
thousand (kilo) bits per second
mbps
million (mega) bits per second
gbps
billion (giga) bits per second

Speeds are quoted in bits, file sizes in bytes: 1 byte = 8 bits.

Fios Internet

There’s fast. Seriously fast. And then don’t even blink kind of fast. Which one fits you?

Download/upload speed in Mbps

File size

Time to download at full speed

Fios options as shown on the slide. File sizes are illustrative; real downloads run slower than the plan’s maximum. Test your internet speed: http://www.speedtest.net/

INSY 2299 · Session 12
Layer 2 · TCP/IP

Internet speed is important for businesses

According to Cloudflare, a two-second delay in website load time leads to…

…a 4 % loss in satisfaction ↓

…a 4.3 % loss in revenue per visitor ($) ↓

Other applications with a need for speed

  • High-frequency trading (1 microsecond advantage ~ $100M annual advantage)
  • Telemedicine (medical imaging 100Mbps+, emergency response: <100ms latency)
  • Smart factory (real-time monitoring: <10ms latency)
  • Self-driving cars (at 60 mph: 1ms latency = 2.7 cm travel, 100ms latency = 2.7 meters travel)
or press →. Ask first: why would a business care?

Self-driving car: distance travelled before it reacts

https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/cdn/what-is-a-cdn/

Layer 3 – Applications to Communicate (WWW and Email)

INSY 2299 · Session 12
Layer 3 · Applications

Layer 3 – Foundations of communication: IP address and DNS

All the devices on the internet have an IP address, which is just a number. IP address: value to identify device connected to the internet.

The domain name service (DNS) is a distributed database that looks up the host and domain names that you enter and returns the actual IP address for the computer that you want to communicate with.

or press →. Check your own IP: https://test-ipv6.com/

INSY 2299 · Session 12
Layer 3 · Applications

Layer 3 – Applications: HTTP (World Wide Web)

Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)

Application transfer protocol that allows Web browsers and Web servers to communicate with each other.

Don’t confuse it with…

Hypertext Markup Language (HTML)

Language used to compose (render) Web pages.

HTTP is the envelope and the conversation (request, response). HTML is the content inside the response that the browser turns into a page.

INSY 2299 · Session 12







  
Layer 3 · Applications

  
Internet and World Wide Web (WWW) are NOT the same thing

  

    

      

        
The World Wide Web is one of the things you can do on the Internet.

        
Internet
Connected computers for sharing information using a certain set of rules (TCP/IP protocol)

        
World Wide Web (WWW)
Application for sharing information built on top of the Internet. Uses the HTTP protocol that allows Web browsers and Web servers to communicate with each other.

        
…and the Web shares the Internet with the other applications: e-mail, file transfer, internet telephony.

        
or press →

Business implications

  
Net neutrality

  

    
Anyone heard of the term “Net Neutrality”?

  

  
INSY 2299 · Session 12







  
Business implications

  
Net neutrality: principle that all Internet traffic should be treated equally

  

    

      
    
      
  • Access providers (ISPs, such as Verizon or Comcast) wanted to offer varying coverage to users, depending on the service used and bandwidth consumed.
    • 
      
  • ISPs wanted to move away from flat-rate pricing toward usage-based pricing.
    • 
      
  • Internet content providers (e.g., Netflix) worry that without strong neutrality rules, ISPs may block content or favor their own offerings above rivals.
    • 
    

      
    

    

      
Illustration

      

      

    

    
Title I regulation: enhance information services. Title II regulation: common carrier (subject to more regulations). Additional information on net neutrality: http://www.nytimes.com/video/technology/100000002881329/how-net-neutrality-works.html
